messages.subject: prior for the intercept
parts:
I have the following Weibull model with only an intercept. I would like to assign a normal distribution with mean 0 and precision 0.0001 as prior for the intercept and a gamma prior Gamma(1,0.0001) for the parameter alpha .
I specified the prior for log alpha using control.data: control.data=list(prior="loggamma",param=c(1,0.0001))).
I think the prior for the intercept can be specified using control.fixed option. I was able to specify the mean and the precision for the intercept  but I do not know what is the default distribution and how can I change it to another distribution different than the default one.
I tried to use prior="normal" inside the control.fixed option but I got an error.
 
n = 1000
alpha = 1.5
eta = 1
lambda = exp(eta)
y = rweibull(n, shape= alpha, scale= lambda^(1/-alpha))
event = rep(1,n)
data = list(y=y, event=event)
formula=inla.surv(y,event)~ 1
model=inla(formula, family ="weibull", data=data,control.fixed = list(mean.intercept=0,prec.intercept = 0.0001), control.data=list(prior="loggamma",param=c(1,0.0001)))
summary(model)
 
Thank you,
Georgiana

messages.author: 13c089061b9212a0
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] prior for the intercept
parts:
Hi,

The default distribution for the fixed effects (which includes the intercept) is Normal. As far as I know, you can change the mean and the precision as you did, but not the Normal distribution.

Best,
Thiago
